_about: LifeFlow's house open models (owner, 2026-11-27: when we use open models, always the same ones we train, so every generation also adds to training). The planner refuses other open models unless a job says why.

image.why: Apache-2.0, in the Higgsfield catalog, runs on the cheapest GPU (L40S), fast, and the catalog supports LoRAs on it.

lora.name: lifeflow-look
lora.teaches: the skylings as 3D cube toys, the app's sky palette, our pixel icons, LifeFlow's light

video.why: Apache-2.0, in the catalog, the most recommended commercially safe open video model; the catalog runs LoRAs on Wan I2V.

lora.name: lifeflow-motion
lora.teaches: how the skylings move and the studio's camera language

dataset.where: /workspace/lifeflow-dataset on the Higgsfield GPU storage (persists across boxes), mirrored in marketing/studio/dataset/ (captions, sources)
what_goes_in: every approved open-model output with its prompt, seed and model (generation adds to training)
studio renders of the skylings from many angles and poses: the code makes perfect, labelled training pictures for free
real app captures for anything UI-like (never used to fake the app; only to teach the look of our world)
dataset.never: user data, real people's faces without consent, anything from another brand or game

training: A LoRA run needs the owner's yes and a cost cap (gpu/planner.mjs prices it). Then the house model + the newest LoRA is the default for every open-model job.
